page: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-32GB is a general-purpose cloud instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 9575F processors clocked at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The system is provisioned with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled as a 300 GB SSD, accompanied by 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. There are no discrete GPU accelerators on this instance.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capabilities, with the stress-ng single-core test (3670.47) and single-threaded bzip3 decompression (17.43 GB/sec) both reaching the top 10% tier. Multi-core compute performance sits in the middle 50% band across multiple suites, including stress-ng multi-core (22341.89), Geekbench multi-core (8800.0), and PassMark CPU (16080.40). Large-block memory bandwidth reaches 114.8 GB/sec for read-only operations and 50.98 GB/sec for writes, though PassMark memory scored in the bottom 10% (1019.02). CPU-based LLM inference reflects these memory and compute constraints, delivering average throughput on small 135M models (179.18 tokens/sec generation) but dropping to the bottom 25% on 7B models (8.4 tokens/sec generation).

Given its balanced CPU-to-memory configuration and 300 GB local SSD, the instance yields steady resource density for multi-tenant or concurrent business applications without dedicated hardware overhead. The primary tradeoff lies in the shared vCPU model and limited memory throughput under synthetic memory benchmarks, which constrains heavily serialized memory-bound tasks. This server fits general web serving (achieving 13.06 GB/sec static throughput), Redis caching (8.37 million SET operations/sec), build environments, and relational database hosting.
description: UpCloud PREMIUM-8xCPU-32GB is a general-purpose KVM cloud instance powered by 8 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. It offers 32.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per vCPU), a bundled 300 GB SSD, and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address, without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations show top-decile single-core CPU execution via stress-ng (3670.47) alongside solid mid-tier multi-core performance (Geekbench multi-core score of 8800.0 and PassMark CPU score of 16080.40). Memory bandwidth reaches 114.8 GB/sec on uncached large reads, although PassMark memory testing registers in the lower tier. Yielding reliable static web serving at 13.06 GB/sec and 8.37 million Redis SET operations per second, this instance is suitable for web serving, application middleware, CI/CD compilation, and mid-tier databases.
